world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: Evidence for the Northern Mam weight scale comes from forms such as in (1); these examples, and all subsequent data, come from original consultant work with speakers from the Todos Santos variety of Mam, a Northern Mam dialect. In Todos Santos Mam, like other Northern varieties, stress is placed on the rightmost heaviest rime type available in the word. There is no secondary stress. [...] When all syllables in a word are equally heavy, stress is rightmost (2). However, final light syllables never get stress; when words consist of all light syllables, stress falls on the penultimate syllable (3)
new_statements.citation: Elkins, Noah & Jennifer Kuo. 2023. A prominence account of the Northern Mam weight hierarchy. Proceedings of the Annual Meetings on Phonology 10 (Supplemental proceedings of AMP 2022). doi:10.3765/amp.v10i0.5433.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Todos Santos (Northern) Mam: primary stress goes to the rightmost syllable of the heaviest rime type present, on the scale VV > Vʔ > VC > V (e.g. [kuʔ.ˈwaːl] 'child', [ˈaːl.q'aʔn] 'robs', [ˈχɪʔ.ʈʂ'ɐχ] 'thin person', [ma.ˈsat] 'deer', [ˈʔoχ.ʈʂɐ] 'before'); ties among non-light syllables go to the final syllable ([tow.ˈsant] 'todosantero'); a final light (open short) syllable is never stressed, so all-light words are penultimate ([ˈme.ɓɐ] 'orphan', [χapaˈninɐ] 'reason'). No word has two VV or two Vʔ syllables. Same system as Ixtahuacán Mam (England 1983:37-38) per Elkins 2023:209; Canger 1969:183 independently states for Todos Santos that strong stress falls 'on the last syllable containing a central that is not ə or a latent central'.
new_statements.exceptions: None lexical. Non-finality: final light syllables never stressed (all-light words penultimate). Elkins 2023:71-72: the voice suffixes -'n (DS) and -n (AP) fail to surface after roots with a heavy nucleus (VV or Vʔ), reappearing when further suffixes/enclitics follow. England's Northern-Mam rule (1975/1990) adds that enclitics never take stress; Elkins & Kuo do not discuss clitics.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level primary stress; Elkins 2023:211 states the prosodic word (ω) is the domain of primary stress assignment, with pitch-accent type varying by word shape and separate phrase-edge boundary tones. Examples are citation forms from elicitation with Todos Santos speakers (Los Angeles/Oakland and Todos Santos).
new_statements.identity_note: mamt1235 is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for retired ISO 639-3 mvj 'Todos Santos Cuchumatán Mam', merged into mam (Glottolog mamm1241) in 2009 because it names a dialect; the earlier catalog pass ruled this key DUPLICATE of mamm1241. The sources quoted here (Elkins & Kuo 2023; Elkins 2023; Canger 1969) describe exactly the Todos Santos Cuchumatán (Huehuetenango) variety, a Northern Mam dialect, whose stress system they state is essentially identical to Ixtahuacán (Northern) Mam as described by England 1975/1983 — i.e. the same rule already coded on mamm1241. Note the language-level contrast: Southern Mam (e.g. Ostuncalco, Cajolá) has fixed penultimate and Western Mam (Tacaná) fixed final stress (England 1990:225; Elkins 2023:209), so the weight-sensitive reading is specific to Northern Mam incl. Todos Santos.

sources.quote: Evidence for the Northern Mam weight scale comes from forms such as in (1); these examples, and all subsequent data, come from original consultant work with speakers from the Todos Santos variety of Mam, a Northern Mam dialect. In Todos Santos Mam, like other Northern varieties, stress is placed on the rightmost heaviest rime type available in the word. There is no secondary stress. [...] When all syllables in a word are equally heavy, stress is rightmost (2). However, final light syllables never get stress; when words consist of all light syllables, stress falls on the penultimate syllable (3)
sources.note: All data from Todos Santos Mam consultants. p.1: 'In Todos Santos Mam, like other Northern varieties, stress is placed on the rightmost heaviest rime type available in the word. There is no secondary stress.' Weight scale VV > Vʔ > VC > V with exemplars (1a-f); p.2: equal (non-light) weight -> rightmost (2); final light syllables never stressed, all-light words -> penultimate (3); no word has two long vowels or two Vʔ syllables. Southern Mam regularly penultimate, Western Mam regularly ultimate (citing England 2017). fn.3 p.6: England 1983 based on Ixtahuacán Mam.

sources.citation: Elkins, Noah Eli. 2023. The interplay of syntax and prosody in Mam. PhD dissertation, University of California, Los Angeles. 359 pp. (eScholarship qt9mc841pp)
sources.note: Todos Santos Mam is the descriptive focus (ch.2 'A grammatical sketch of Todos Santos Mam'). sec. 2.3 'Stress', printed pp.70-71: 'In Northern Mam, stress is not fixed, but is still predictable, falling on the heaviest rime type available within a word. The Northern Mam weight hierarchy for assigning stress is VV > Vʔ > VC > V... if all syllables have equivalent weight, the final syllable is stressed, but stress retracts to penultimate position if a final light syllable would be stressed', exx. (4a-e) Todos Santos Mam; stress conditions surfacing of voice suffixes -'n/-n. Part II sec. 2.3.2 '…

sources.citation: England, Nora C. 1975. Mam grammar in outline. PhD dissertation, University of Florida (sec. 1.3 Stress, pp.35-36; Ixtahuacán Mam).
sources.note: General (Ixtahuacán, Northern) Mam rule already coded on mamm1241: stress on the long vowel; else vowel before the last glottal stop; else vowel before the last root consonant; never on suffixes unless they contain VV or ʔ. Not Todos Santos data.

sources.citation: England, Nora C. 1990. El Mam: semejanzas y diferencias regionales. In N. C. England & S. R. Elliott (comps.), Lecturas sobre la lingüística maya, 221-252. Antigua Guatemala: CIRMA.
sources.note: sec. 1.2.3 Acento, pp.225-226: three stress systems within Mam — Tacaná final, Ostuncalco penultimate, Ixtahuacán heavy syllable (long vowel, else last vowel + glottal stop, else last root syllable closed by a consonant; never on enclitics). Todos Santos is not mentioned in the stress section.

sources.citation: Godfrey, Thomas James & Wesley M. Collins. 1987. Una encuesta dialectal en el área mam de Guatemala. Guatemala: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano. xxii+415 pp.
sources.note: Survey point 22 Todos Santos Cuchumatán, printed pp.87-88: lists three extra phonemes, lexical differences, vowel addition/omission; no stress statement for Todos Santos (stress remarks exist only for other towns, e.g. Comitancillo penultimate, San Martín Sacatepéquez final). Appendix 6 gives stress-marked phonetic transcriptions of the 80 test sentences per survey point (data, no rule).
